probes.support_reason: F-1: every numbered sub-requirement is delivered. (1) `fn mid(v: std.ArrayList(i32)) i32 { return v.items[1]; }` is a function with one parameter of Zig's normal growable-integer-sequence type and a body that returns the element at index 1 of that parameter. (2) `var xs: std.ArrayList(i32) = .empty;` followed by `try xs.appendSlice(allocator, &.{ 1, 2, 3 });` binds a local `xs` to such a sequence containing 1, 2, 3 — std.ArrayList in Zig 0.16 is the unmanaged list, so the allocator is supplied per call and `.empty` is the documented empty initializer. (3) `const y = mid(xs);` binds the call's result in Zig's normal binding form. (4) `return y;`. F-2: language and bundled std only. F-3: builds and runs under the frozen semantic-compression recipe unmodified and prints 2. F-4: no extra flag, package or code generation. F-6: no clause of the language reference or of the std documentation places std.ArrayList, `.empty`, `appendSlice`, `items` or `try` under a normative prohibition or deprecation. R10 form selection: `var xs: std.ArrayList(i32) = .empty;` + `try xs.appendSlice(allocator, &.{1,2,3});` is 31 tokens; the alternative `var buf = [_]i32{1,2,3};` + `var xs: std.ArrayList(i32) = .fromOwnedSlice(&buf);` is 33 tokens, so R10 selects the measured form. A `[]i32` slice parameter was rejected under R1, not R10: a slice is not the growable-sequence type the canonical task names. HARNESS DISCLOSURE (spec 10.4, not a support deduction): Zig has no nested function declarations — a `fn` item may only appear at container scope — so `mid`'s declaration cannot be placed inside the enclosing function body next to the call site. Exactly one scaffold token, the `}` that closes the enclosing `probe` function, therefore falls inside the marked region so that the region stays contiguous as tokenizer rule R1 requires. This is the identical layout the frozen Java fragment for this probe uses for the identical reason, and it is the minimum possible: every alternative layout puts a whole function header (12 tokens) inside the region instead.

probes.support_reason: F-1: every numbered sub-requirement is delivered. (1) `fn divmod2(a: i32, b: i32) struct { i32, i32 }` takes two signed 32-bit integer parameters and produces both the truncating quotient and the remainder from a single call, using Zig's normal multiple-result mechanism — an anonymous tuple type, which the reference documents as the way a function returns more than one value. (2) `const q, const r = divmod2(7, 3);` binds the two results to two separate locals in ONE binding construct: Zig has destructuring assignment, so the 'if the language has one' clause is satisfied rather than approximated. (3) `return q + r;`. R10/R1 selection among the three: @divExact fails R1 (it is undefined when the division is not exact, so it does not compute 'the integer quotient' for general operands); @divFloor and @divTrunc tie at 7 tokens, and R1 selects @divTrunc with @rem because the canonical task names the results `a/b` and `a%b`, which in every other language of the fixed comparison set truncate toward zero and take the sign of the dividend — choosing @divFloor/@mod would make the Zig fragment produce -3 and 2 where the other nine produce -2 and -1, and R1 requires the same stated outputs. F-2/F-3/F-4: language and bundled std only; builds and runs under the frozen recipe and prints 3; no extra flag. F-6: no normative prohibition or deprecation applies to tuple types, destructuring, @divTrunc or @rem. HARNESS DISCLOSURE: as at F06.P1, one scaffold token — the `}` closing the enclosing function — lies inside the marked region because Zig has no nested function declarations and the region must be contiguous under R1.

hidden_items.why: Local site `return .{ @divTrunc(a, b), @rem(a, b) };` inside `divmod2`, whose parameters the canonical task declares as unconstrained i32. Sub-test H8a fires: for the same operand types the outcome at the edge — a zero divisor, and @divTrunc(minInt(i32), -1) — differs by build mode. Zig 0.16.0 Language Reference, 'Undefined Behavior' — the listed cases (Integer Overflow, Division by Zero, Index out of Bounds) are SAFETY-CHECKED undefined behaviour: the compiler emits a check that panics in Debug and ReleaseSafe, while in ReleaseFast and ReleaseSmall the behaviour is undefined. The local tokens `@divTrunc` and `@rem` fix the ROUNDING and the SIGN of the result (that half is counted as a local fact above) but select nothing about the edge, so the LED test of methodology 04 section 1.2 fails for the edge behaviour. Counted ONCE for this local site: the panic-versus-undefined rule is a single normative statement of the reference covering overflow, division by zero and out-of-bounds alike, so under methodology 04 section 1.3.2 the two builtins at one site are one event. H5 was considered and NOT counted separately for the same behaviour: the single-assignment rule of section 1.3.1 gives one event exactly one item, and section 1.2.1's mandatory illustration places 'an arithmetic outcome at overflow that differs between build configurations' in H8a. RECONCILIATION with this probe's determinacy record, which reports B = 1 with 'cannot fail': the two metrics apply different tests and the difference is deliberate. Semantic Determinacy enumerates interpretations of the measured region as written, and the region's only CALL passes the literals 7 and 3, so no completion of the program reaches a zero divisor. Hidden Semantic Cost asks whether the behaviour is signalled at the use site over the probe's declared input domain, and the canonical task declares `divmod2`'s parameters as unconstrained signed 32-bit integers, which is the domain the DECLARED function must be read against. Neither reading is used to lower the other metric.

Local site `return q + r;`. A distinct local site, so a distinct event under methodology 04 section 1.3.2. The same rule applies: signed integer overflow of `+` is safety-checked undefined behaviour, panicking in Debug/ReleaseSafe and undefined in ReleaseFast/ReleaseSmall, and no token at the site selects which. Zig DOES provide edge-selecting operators — `+%` wraps and `+|` saturates (Zig 0.16.0 Language Reference, 'Operators') — so this is a genuine choice the author did not make here, not an absence of the facility; writing `+` is what the canonical task's 'ordinary operators' requires.

Witness semantic-compression/witnesses/zig/chunk_B/f07p1_C1_signed.zig (a = 2147483647, b = 1, c = 0 as i32, measured region byte-identical): builds under the frozen recipe and prints 2147483647.

CLASS 2 - typed UNSIGNED fixed-width integer operands (u8 ... u128). Materially different from class 1 on dimension 8 (signedness and width of the value produced) and dimension 9 (observable result): the same written statement on u8 operands has a different representable range and therefore a different outcome for the same numerals. Witness semantic-compression/witnesses/zig/chunk_B/f07p1_C2_unsigned.zig (a = 200, b = 1, c = 56 as u8): builds under the frozen recipe and traps at run time with `panic: integer overflow`, where the i32 rendering of the same numerals produces 256.

CLASS 3 - binary floating-point operands (f16/f32/f64/f80/f128). A4 = binary floating point; A10 = IEEE-754 rounding, with infinities and NaN instead of a trap. Materially different from classes 1 and 2 on dimensions 8 and 9. Witness semantic-compression/witnesses/zig/chunk_B/f07p1_C3_float.zig (a = 2.5, b = 2.0, c = 0.5 as f64): builds and prints 5.5. Both families are FOLDED into classes 1-3 rather than counted separately, because methodology 03 Rule 1.4.6 confines an unbounded family of completions to the closed outcome classes of section 1.4 that it can realize, and neither reaches a class those three do not. The fold is the anti-inflation direction and is disclosed rather than silently dropped.

CLASS 4 - all three operands are comptime-known constants of type `comptime_int`. The whole expression is then evaluated at compile time with ARBITRARY precision and `r` is itself `comptime_int`; overflow cannot occur at the operation. Materially different from class 1 on dimension 9. Witness semantic-compression/witnesses/zig/chunk_B/f07p1_C4_comptime_int.zig (`const a = 2147483647; const b = 2; const c = 0;`, measured region byte-identical): builds under the frozen recipe and prints 4294967294, where the i32 rendering of the same numerals traps.
